description.narrative:
During the activity period 1st of January 2024 until 31st of December 2027 the project will work with several goals.
The four main outcomes
- Formal and non formal social and health services - which means social service providers from the state or civil society organizations - strengthen social inclusion for children and youth with disabilities by utilizing resources and practices from Save the Children's international methods and thematic approaches.
- Mothers of children in rural areas and youth with disabilities have increased skills and knowledge within the field - such as the rights of services and possibilities for a better life. Youth will also have better possibilities for decent employment
- Save the children collaborates with and supports children to engage with the Ombudsman and Office for Good Governance in the development of the new Strategy for Children's Rights and the Action Plan for the next period, 2024-26.
- Children and youth in Kosovo contribute to the protection and sustainability of biodiversity in the country. They will also have better access to the national parks.
The main reasons for the decision to support the project
- Sida has identified that the need for increased social inclusion for children with disabilities and their families in Kosovo is vast.
- The project correlates with Kosovo's National Development Strategy 2030, several of the Sustainable Development Goals of Agenda 2030 and the Strategy for Sweden's Reform Cooperation with the Western Balkans 2021-2027.
- The projects aim is to enhance Non Governmental Organizations capacity to enable them to provide qualitative service.
- The organisation is a strong actor within the field of children's rights and advocacy and has good contact with other organizations, communities and the state. Their work and network is broad and connects to different societal levels.
- Since 2022 they have reached a status of National Office, which implies that they have strengthened their organization.

De främsta huvudsakliga målen:
- Civilsamhällesorganisationer som leverar vård och offentliga vårdleverantörer ska stärka social inkludering för barn och ungdomar med funktionsvariationer genom att få tillgång till och använda sig av Rädda Barnens tematiska tillvägagångssätt och praxis.
- Mödrar till barn med funktionsvariation på landsbygden och ungdomar med funktionsvariationer ska få ökade kunskaper om sina rättigheter samt färdigheter inom området. Ungdomarna ska även få möjligheter till en anständig och trygg anställning.
- Rädda barnen ska stödja barn att engagera sig med Ombudsmannem och Office for Good Governance vad gäller utvecklingen av den nya strategin för barns rättigheter och handlingsplanen för perioden 2024-2026.
- Barn och ungdomar i Kosovo bidrar till skyddet av biologisk mångfald i landet genom att lära sig om skyddsmekanismer och hållbarhet. De ska även få möjlighet att bättre ta vara på Kosovos nationalparker.

The overall objective for the project is - Enhancing social inclusion of children, especially those with disabilities, and parents/caregivers in Kosovo through improved social services and active involvement in child rights and biodiversity project. To reach the objective, Save the Children have outlined four outcomes that are presented below.
- Formal and non-formal social (which Sida considers should be mentioned as public services and Non-governmental organizations) and health services providers strengthen social inclusion for children and youth with disabilities by utilizing resources and practices from Save the Children's thematic approaches.
- Mothers of children in rural areas and youth with disabilities have increased skills, knowledge, and opportunities for decent employment.
- Save the children in Kosovo collaborates with and supports children to engage with Ombudsperson Institution and Office for Good Governance in the development of the new national Strategy for Children's Rights and the Action Plan for the next period, 2024-26.
- Children and youth in Kosovo contribute to the protection and sustainability of biodiversity in the country.

description.narrative:
The project in 2025 advanced social inclusion and protection of children in Kosovo, especially those with disabilities, through coordinated efforts in service delivery, policy support, economic empowerment, child participation, and environmental education.
The project strengthened collaboration with key institutions by developing a standardized case management training module with the Ministry of Justice, aimed at improving service quality across all municipalities and ensuring sustainability through the Professional Council for Social and Family Services accreditation framework. It also built the capacity of 35 social assistance providers, enhancing implementation of the reformed Social Assistance Scheme and improving services for vulnerable groups. In parallel, the project supported the development of key Administrative Instructions to operationalize the Law on Social and Family Services.
In 2025, the project enhanced the capacities of 50 social, health, and education service providers through Safe Families training. The trainings improved knowledge on child rights, safeguarding, positive parenting, gender equality, and inclusion, promoting nonviolent discipline and better support for families. They also introduced the Respect My Body handbook to raise awareness on childrens rights, boundaries, and protection from abuse.
During 2025 no implementation activities were initiated under Output 1.3. However, a Memorandum of Understanding with the Ministry of Health was initiated to formalize cooperation and define the scope of support, and is currently under review. Political instability and internal restructuring within the Ministry of Health delayed progress and may affect timely cooperation and implementation.
Support to the employability of mothers of children from Early Childhood Care and Development Centers was provided by facilitating access to vocational training. Participants gained practical skills in areas such as business management and catering. Early results include two women securing employment, demonstrating the initiatives impact on skills development and labour market access.
During the reporting year, the project strengthened disability inclusion in vocational education and training by completing the revision of the Vocational Training Center (VTC) Manual in partnership with the Employment Agency of the Republic of Kosovo. The updated manual introduced two key issues, the Individual Professional Training Plan and the Adjustments Plan for Individuals Requiring Specific Adjustments, equipping 28 VTC professionals with structured guidance to adapt learning environments, teaching methods, and assistive support to meet the needs of youth with disabilities.
In 2025, children from Child-Led Groups and Child-Led Municipal Assemblies were supported to participate in national consultations on priorities for the new National Strategy on the Rights of the Child (20262031) and its Action Plan. Inclusion was further ensured through a dedicated online consultation with a Serbian CLG from northern municipalities, with their recommendations formally submitted to the Office of Good Governance.
Through a Memorandum of Understanding, KEPA and SwEPA supported SCiK in educating children and youth on biodiversity and the protection of natural parks, while SCiK contributed by promoting the inclusion of childrens perspectives in protection of national parks and biodiversity. In partnership with the Utalaya Foundation, the project also delivered an inclusive fiveday Summer School reaching 43 children from diverse backgrounds. The programme focused on experiential learning and peer mentorship, fostering environmental awareness, sustainability, inclusion, and leadership skills.
A child representative was supported to participate in the first European Child Participation Fair, facilitating exchange on meaningful child participation practices, while the Young Voices methodology was presented as an effective approach to ensuring child participation.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
